prompts.text: Which relative do you understand better now than you did five years ago?
A cousin joins our family chat after years away. What introduction would help them feel included?
Tell us about a relative whose first impression of you turned out to be wrong.
Who in our family notices when somebody needs company, even before they ask?
Learn a relative's favourite joke or hear how they met their closest friend?
We sometimes know a relative's daily routine better than their interests. Whose interests would you like to hear about?
What do you wish we asked about your life beyond work or school?
Giving relatives room to change helps a family stay close. Where have you seen this happen?
Which pair of relatives gets along despite having different personalities?
We swap our usual jobs at the next gathering. Which role would help you appreciate somebody else's effort?
Who would you ask to explain a confusing family connection, knowing they won't tease you for asking?
Describe a moment when a younger relative helped you see an older one differently.
Which family relationship grew through a shared interest nobody expected?
Spend an afternoon learning a relative's hobby or let them try yours?
What do people in our family often guess incorrectly about your personality?
Two siblings sometimes describe the same household differently. What did each of you notice most?
A relative says they miss us but dislikes large gatherings. What smaller plan would suit them?
Who do you turn to for practical help, and who do you turn to for a listening ear?
Tell us about a time you learnt a relative had been quietly recommending your work to other people.
Which small responsibility taught you something about caring for another person?
Family closeness does not always follow the family tree. Which unexpected bond have you enjoyed watching grow?
How do you prefer us to introduce you to people who only know you through family stories?
Our usual organiser wants to enjoy a gathering without managing it. How would we divide the work?
Which relative knows a side of you the rest of us seldom see?
Ask an elder about a friendship from their youth or ask a younger relative about their current friends?
What makes a visit feel relaxed rather than like an occasion you need to prepare for?
When did a relative make you feel welcome in a place where you knew nobody else?
Whose way of showing excitement differs most from yours?
Some relatives show care by fixing things; others stay for a chat. Which gestures do you notice first?
Somebody new to the family asks whom to sit beside at dinner. What would you tell them about each of us?
What have you learnt about a relative from seeing them around their friends?
How do you recognise when a family joke has stopped being funny for the person involved?
Hear the story behind a relative's proudest photograph or see an object they keep for sentimental reasons?
Which family role have you grown out of, even if people still associate it with you?
Tell us about a time you enjoyed a relative's company without doing anything special.
A relative starts a hobby nobody here understands. Which questions would help us show interest?
What helps you feel like an adult around people who remember you as a child?
A quiet relative deserves an invitation without pressure to perform. What makes an invitation feel comfortable?
Who surprises you most when they become enthusiastic about a subject?
What do you enjoy doing with one relative which wouldn't work as well with the whole family?
We often ask who somebody resembles before asking what they enjoy. What would you prefer people noticed about you?
Two relatives want to reconnect after a long silence, with no argument behind it. What first plan would feel easy?
Describe a time a family member took your suggestion seriously when you expected them to dismiss it.
Which difference between generations has become easier for you to understand?
Share an ordinary weekday with a relative or join them for an event they look forward to all year?
Who in our family would you like to spend time with outside the usual gathering?
Respect for an elder and curiosity about their views work well together. What have you enjoyed asking an elder?
What do we misunderstand when we mistake your quietness for a bad mood?
A relative's friend mentions they know you through a story you have never heard. Which story would you hope it was?
Which of your interests would surprise relatives who haven't seen you recently?
Tell us about learning something from a relative through doing a task together.
What tells you a relative wants advice rather than company?
Family conversations sometimes centre on whoever has the biggest news. What ordinary news would you enjoy sharing today?
Get a relative's honest opinion on a small decision or hear what they would do differently in your position?
Which personality trait do you share with a relative you don't physically resemble?
Our family plans a day out with different walking speeds and energy levels. What would make everyone feel considered?
What has helped you maintain a connection with a relative whose schedule rarely matches yours?
Describe a time somebody in the family remembered a preference you hadn't mentioned for ages.
Whose patience have you come to appreciate through spending more time together?
Being available to help differs from wanting to make every decision. How do you like people to offer help?
Which relative asks questions you enjoy answering?
We each explain an interest without using its usual jargon. What would you talk about, and who would you ask to go next?
What part of your personality comes out during family games?
Invite a relative on an errand you usually do alone or join them for one of theirs?
We learn different things about people in a kitchen, on a journey and at a table. Where have you understood a relative better?
Who has changed your mind about what two relatives of different ages might have in common?
Tell us about a time you introduced two family members to a shared interest.
How do you prefer us to ask about a new person in your life?
A relative shares good news but wants to keep the details private for now. How would you celebrate within those limits?
Which relative has a sense of humour you appreciate more as you get older?
A family nickname needs room for the person to outgrow it. How do you feel about yours?
What makes it easier to ask us for a small favour?
Have a relative teach you something slowly or let them watch while you try and ask questions?
Describe a moment when a relative's encouragement helped you attempt something unfamiliar.
Who in our family approaches a familiar problem in a way you wouldn't have considered?
We need to choose a film for three generations. Which question would narrow the options without assuming everyone's taste?
Who helps you work out whether a family message needs a reply from everyone or only from its recipient?
A relative's reputation sometimes stays the same after their habits change. Whose recent changes deserve more attention?
Who would you choose for a conversation about something you both find puzzling?
Plan a visit around one person's favourite activity or let each person choose one small part?
Tell us about a time a relative gave you space and stayed connected.
Which family member has a way of disagreeing you find helpful?
Someone misses a gathering because they need rest. What message would show we thought of them without making them feel guilty?
What would make you more comfortable suggesting a change to a family plan?
Knowing a relative for years doesn't remove the need to ask what they prefer now. What preference of yours has changed?
When two relatives explain the same message differently, how do you check what the sender meant?
A familiar greeting often carries an expectation to stop and chat. How do we signal when we are happy to talk but short on time?
Hear a relative describe you in three qualities or ask them which shared experience they remember most?
Which relative brings out your curiosity rather than your need to have an answer?
Describe an ordinary moment when you realised a younger relative had become someone you learn from.
Our family starts a shared project with no appointed leader. What would help different voices shape it?
What does a thoughtful goodbye after a visit look like to you?
Catching up works better when nobody has to prove how busy they've been. What would you enjoy discussing instead?
Whose company feels different in a small group compared with a large gathering?
Receive a short update while a relative travels or hear their whole story once they return?
How would you like us to respond when you say you'd rather observe than join an activity?
Tell us about a family conversation which continued in your thoughts after everyone went home.
We each get to ask one relative a question we've never thought to ask before. Whom would you choose, and what would you ask?
What small change would help our conversations feel less predictable?
Relatives sometimes become friends through the ordinary time between family occasions. What ordinary time would you like us to share?
